newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT ENDS AT $19 AS U.S. GASOLINE RALLIES.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT ENDS AT $19 AS U.S. GASOLINE RALLIES.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures reversed early losses to close 15 cents higher on Wednesday on the back of a rally in U.S. NYMEX gasoline, brokers said.
September IPE last traded at $19.00 a barrel, 15 cents off the high, after a rally late in what had been a lacklustre session ranging around $18.80 to $18.90.
The London surge was a response to a break by September WTI above resistance at $20.00 a barrel to a high of $20.30. The U.S. crude front month later fell back to $20.18.
The crude rally in turn was triggered by a determined jump in U.S. unleaded gasoline, fired up by bullish stock and demand data and refinery problems.
September gasoline was 2.29 cent higher at 66.00 a gallon.
"It was gasoline all the way, helped by the APIs and the DoEs," a broker said.
The U.S. Department of Energy on Wednesday put U.S. gasoline stocks off 1.5 million barrels in the week to August 8. It put gasoline demand 2.7 percent higher at 8.43 million barrels per day (bpd).
Implied gasoline demand in the American Petroleum Institute data remained firmly above eight million bpd at a strong 8.2 million bpd.
U.S. gasoline was also supported by strong New York Habor cash values and problems in a catalytic cracker at Exxon Corp's Baytown plant in Houston, Texas.
Exxon said the 110,000 bpd Number 3 cracker was taken down for an indeterminate time. A source also said the plant had also scheduled a major turnround for January.
The London crude rally saw October Brent smashing through chart resistance at $18.95. October last traded at $19.14.
Key resistance on Thursday for front month Brent was put by one broker at $19.15 with initial support at $18.80.
